evaluated.name: Weakest-link investment restraint and liquidity coverage
evaluated.expression: MIN(ZSCORE(NEG(GROWTH(ppegt, 1))), ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(oancf, lct), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Expected returns are governed by the weaker of two conditions — restraint in irreversible capacity building and the ability of operating cash flow to cover near-term obligations — so a firm scores well only if it is simultaneously disciplined in hard-asset investment and internally solvent.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the financing-source decomposition of asset growth and instead uses a non-separable MIN (weakest-link) form on two standardized channels, which cannot be reproduced by any linear combination of the investment and quality legs. Because both inputs are z-scores and MIN is monotone in each argument, the ordering is sign-stable and immune to the rank-product inversion problem: two low inputs give a low, not a high, score, and a firm that is restrained but illiquid is correctly ranked with the illiquid group.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Internal cash coverage of investment
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(oancf, 3), TS_SUM(capx, 3)), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms whose three-year operating cash flow comfortably covers three-year capital expenditure are funding investment out of proven earnings power, whereas firms investing far in excess of internal cash generation must lean on external capital and subsequently underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This removes the raw, outlier-dominated GROWTH term and the internally inconsistent 2× multiplier: the denominator (cumulative capex) is non-negative and smoothed over three years, so the ratio is well behaved and monotone in cash-flow quality per dollar of investment. It is a single scale-free quantity in which investment and quality are inseparable — the same capex level maps to opposite signal values depending on internal cash generation — and it uses the sign convention consistently across shrinking and expanding firms.

evaluated.name: Inventory glut in below-industry-margin firms
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(TS_RANK(RATIO(invt, sale), 5)), INDICATOR(NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale))), 0))
evaluated.hypothesis: Working-capital investment is a warning sign only when the firm's inventory-to-sales position sits at the high end of its own five-year history and its gross margin is below its industry peers, because weak-margin firms cannot clear excess stock without discounting and future write-downs.
evaluated.reasoning: Instead of one-year inventory growth relative to sales growth plus a margin change (the Abarbanell–Bushee/Thomas–Zhang additive combination the critic flagged), this uses a position-in-own-history state variable for inventory intensity and gates it on an industry-relative margin level, so the construct is a conditional capacity-glut state rather than two stacked published change signals. The INTERACTION_TYPE now matches the expression: the indicator provides genuine conditioning, the industry z-score removes sector composition effects in margins, and the standardized inventory-state leg keeps the ordering sign-stable.

evaluated.name: Cash earnings coverage of capital spending
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(ib, dp), 3), TS_SUM(capx, 3)), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms whose three-year cash earnings comfortably exceed three-year capital expenditure are reinvesting out of proven earnings power, whereas firms spending well beyond internal cash generation are engaged in externally financed, low-quality expansion and subsequently underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the direct coverage repair of the archive's best signal: `ib + dp` is the pre-cash-flow-statement measure of internal funds and is populated decades earlier than `oancf`, so the same funding-discipline mechanism should be estimated on a far larger and longer panel. The denominator (cumulative capex) is non-negative and smoothed, so the ratio is monotone in internal-funding quality per dollar of investment with no sign-flip pathology.

evaluated.name: Gross profit per employee growth
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(GROWTH(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), emp), 1), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: When a firm's investment in labor capacity is rising faster than the gross profit that labor generates, the expansion is unproductive; rising gross profit per employee identifies expansion that is actually creating economic value.
evaluated.reasoning: This opens an entirely new input channel — labor rather than physical or financial capital — where the investment leg (headcount) and the quality leg (gross profit) are fused inside a single productivity ratio, so the signal cannot be replicated by either theme alone. Labor productivity adjusts more slowly than accounting accruals and is not a standard anomaly denominator, so the mispricing is plausibly less arbitraged than capex- or accrual-based versions.

evaluated.name: Improving cash return on installed capital
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), ppegt), 5), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: The productivity of the existing capital stock, not its size or growth rate, distinguishes productive investment from low-quality expansion; firms whose cash earnings per dollar of gross installed capital are on a rising five-year path are compounding capital successfully.
evaluated.reasoning: Scaling cash earnings by gross PP&E rather than total assets makes the denominator a pure cumulative-investment measure, so the ratio is literally the realized return on past investment and the interaction is intrinsic rather than bolted on. Using a five-year TREND rather than a level targets the *state change* in capital productivity, which is what a rational investor would use to judge whether continued investment is warranted, and it is distinct from the level-based profitability factors inside FF5's RMW.

evaluated.name: Sign-flipped capacity expansion by relative profitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(GROWTH(ppegt, 1), 1)), SIGN(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Capacity expansion carries opposite return information depending on the firm's profitability relative to its industry: growth by above-peer-profitability firms reflects genuine opportunity, while identical growth by below-peer firms reflects value-destroying escalation.

evaluated.name: Capital-productivity-weighted capex intensity
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(ppent, COALESCE(intan, 0)))), RATIO(capx, ppent)), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: The same rate of capital spending is value-creating for firms that already generate high gross profit per dollar of invested capital and value-destroying for firms whose existing capital base is unproductive, so investment intensity should be signed and scaled by industry-relative capital productivity.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the acquisition channel entirely — no zero mass point, since capx/ppent is continuously distributed and the productivity leg is defined for essentially all operating firms — and instead measures quality as gross profit per unit of *accumulated investment* including capitalized intangibles, which is not a standard anomaly denominator. The multiplicative form is monotone-safe because the capex leg is non-negative: unproductive expanders sit far negative, productive expanders far positive, and firms that barely invest sit near zero regardless of productivity, which is exactly the economic ordering the mechanism implies.

evaluated.name: Irreversible capital intensity times margin instability
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(ppegt, at), VOL(RATIO(ib, sale), 5)), 1)

evaluated.name: Accrual-adjusted internal funding of capex
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, lct), che), 1)), 3), TS_SUM(capx, 3)), 1)

evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(che, ADD(ib, dp)), ADD(capx, lct)), 1)

The denominator is now the sum of two strictly positive commitment items rather than a near-zero-prone cash stock, so the ordering is stable and monotone in resource adequacy and cash-poor firms no longer populate both tails. evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(che, TS_SUM(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 3)), TS_SUM(capx, 3)), 1)

The quality leg is now cumulative earnings divided by cumulative absolute earnings, a bounded [−1, +1] consistency score in which a modestly but reliably profitable firm scores as highly as a very profitable one — so it is not a profitability level or an RMW proxy, and it is continuous, which avoids both the ZSCORE-centering contradiction and the zero-mass long leg that a raw loss count would create. evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(che, SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1))), ADD(capx, dlc)), 1)

evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(capx, 3), TS_SUM(dp, 3)), 1)

critic_notes.target_name: Debt-financed expansion
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the published decomposition of the asset-growth anomaly by financing source (Cooper–Gulen–Schill combined with the debt-issuance/external-financing anomaly of Spiess–Affleck-Graves and Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan), and the rank-product form is also fragile if RANK is zero-centered, since two low ranks would produce a high product and invert the intended ordering.

critic_notes.target_name: Accrual-financed asset growth
critic_notes.rationale: Total accruals (ib − oancf) are mechanically a large component of asset growth, so this multiplies two heavily overlapping and individually well-documented anomalies (Sloan accruals × asset growth) rather than combining distinct information, and the interaction is likely to be close to a squared version of a single underlying construct.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash-burn amplified growth penalty
critic_notes.rationale: The expression is internally inconsistent with the stated hypothesis because asset growth can be negative, so the 2× multiplier also doubles the *shrinking* cash-burners' signal in the opposite direction, and using raw unranked GROWTH(at,1) leaves the signal outlier-dominated while adding little beyond the plain asset-growth factor.

critic_notes.target_name: Unstable-earnings growth
critic_notes.rationale: Conditioning the investment effect on multi-year ROA volatility is an economically coherent and not-directly-published interaction, though earnings volatility overlaps heavily with distress/idiosyncratic-volatility screens and the 5-year window will cost coverage, so the incremental content over asset growth alone needs to be demonstrated.

critic_notes.target_name: Inventory bloat with eroding margins
critic_notes.rationale: Inventory growth relative to sales growth paired with deteriorating gross margin is almost exactly two of the Abarbanell–Bushee fundamental signals (and Thomas–Zhang inventory growth), and the declared INTERACTION_TYPE "ratio" contradicts the expression, which is an additive rank sum with no conditioning at all.

critic_notes.target_name: Efficient self-funded growth
critic_notes.rationale: The long-leg framing — asset growth measured in turnover units and validated by sustained internal cash generation — is a defensible and less-crowded angle, but both legs are Piotroski F-score components so the novelty is in the multiplicative form, which will need the rank convention checked to avoid rewarding the doubly-low corner.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash earnings coverage of capital spending
critic_notes.rationale: This is the same funding-discipline mechanism as the archive's "Internal cash coverage of investment" with only the internal-funds proxy swapped (ib+dp for oancf), so it is close to a cosmetic variant — but the pre-1988 panel extension is a legitimate, well-motivated coverage repair rather than a fishing variant, and the construction is internally consistent.

critic_notes.target_name: Acquisition intensity per dollar of gross profit
critic_notes.rationale: Acquirer underperformance is a long-documented anomaly and aqc-scaled investment intensity is a standard component of asset-growth/external-financing measures, plus COALESCE(aqc,0) creates a large zero mass point (most firm-years) that makes the entire long leg an arbitrary tie-break among non-acquirers rather than a ranked portfolio.

critic_notes.target_name: High-coverage weakest link of capex restraint and gross profitability
critic_notes.rationale: The diagnostic motivation (separating operator form from thin-sample artifact) is honest and the expression is internally consistent, but both legs are near-direct proxies for FF5's own CMA and RMW factors, so the evaluation metric (FF5 alpha) is largely absorbed by construction and a null result will not cleanly identify whether the MIN structure works.

critic_notes.target_name: Gross profit per employee growth
critic_notes.rationale: Genuinely opens a labor-input channel that fuses investment and quality inside one ratio and is not a restatement of the archive signals, though it partially overlaps the documented hiring-rate/employee-growth anomaly and emp is a coarsely rounded, merger-contaminated annual field that will add noise to a one-year growth rate.

critic_notes.target_name: Improving cash return on installed capital
critic_notes.rationale: Trending cash return on gross installed capital is a defensible, internally consistent state-change measure distinct from the archive's level ratios, but it overlaps the well-known ΔROA/F-score profitability-improvement predictor and the ppegt denominator is unstable for asset-light firms, where small gross PP&E will dominate the trend before winsorization.

critic_notes.target_name: Sign-flipped capacity expansion by relative profitability
critic_notes.rationale: The SIGN construction is internally consistent with the stated hypothesis and correctly fixes the INDICATOR-masking that produced the earlier wrong-signed spread, but the hard discontinuity at the industry median assigns near-random signs to the mass of firms with ROA close to peers, and the long leg's implicit bet that capacity growth predicts *positive* returns among profitable firms runs against the broadly documented negative investment-return relation.

critic_notes.target_name: Capex intensity weighted by relative earnings quality
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the archive's "capital-productivity-weighted capex intensity" with the quality axis swapped from gross profit/capital to smoothed ROA and the scaler from capx/ppent to capx/at — a cosmetic re-parameterization — and because the non-negative capex leg only rescales a signed industry-relative profitability z-score, the cross-sectional ordering is largely a repackaged (well-known) profitability anomaly rather than a genuine interaction.

critic_notes.target_name: Accrual-adjusted internal funding of capex
critic_notes.rationale: A legitimate, well-motivated construction test that isolates the cash-conversion component distinguishing the archive's oancf-based winner from its ib+dp null while extending coverage pre-1988, though it overlaps the archive ratio heavily and the accrual proxy is contaminated because subtracting Δlct treats an increase in short-term debt as improved "cash" coverage (Sloan's definition nets out dlc and txp).

critic_notes.target_name: Capacity growth weighted by relative gross profitability
critic_notes.rationale: Beyond being a two-change variant of the archive's SIGN-based capacity-expansion signal (making attribution impossible), the expression is internally inconsistent with the hypothesis: PP&E growth is frequently negative, so firms that are shrinking capacity *and* have below-peer gross profitability receive the highest scores, which is the opposite of the stated economics.

critic_notes.target_name: Investment funding gap per dollar of cash buffer
critic_notes.rationale: Scaling a signed funding gap by a near-zero-prone cash stock makes the ordering unstable and non-monotone in the intended distress dimension — small-cash firms populate *both* extreme tails, so a cash-poor firm with an internal-funding surplus is ranked as the strongest buy, contradicting the liquidity-buffer story, and the surviving variation is largely the known cash-holdings/investment level effect.

critic_notes.target_name: Incremental sales per dollar of prior-year capex
critic_notes.rationale: The lagged output-response channel is a genuinely new axis relative to the archive's contemporaneous funding and quality gates, but the near-zero capx denominator means the signal will be substantially driven by 1/capx (i.e., the known low-investment effect) plus raw sales growth, so a scaled form such as (Δsale/at)/(capx/at) or a rank transform is needed for the test to be informative.

critic_notes.target_name: Inventory intensity scaled by relative margin
critic_notes.rationale: This targets a concrete, diagnosed defect in the archive's inventory signal — the INDICATOR mask created a degenerate zero-mass long leg and a wrong-signed alpha — and replacing it with a non-negative intensity leg times a continuous industry-neutral margin z-score is a substantive repair, though the resulting signal remains at risk of being dominated by the gross-margin (profitability) leg rather than the inventory interaction.

critic_notes.target_name: Sloan-consistent cash funding of capex
critic_notes.rationale: A genuine measurement fix rather than a cosmetic tweak — excluding cash and short-term debt from the working-capital change makes the numerator a Sloan-consistent cash-generation measure so revolver draws no longer masquerade as internal funding — though the incremental effect of dlc is likely small and the family risks being a repackaging of the accruals plus investment anomalies already spanned by CMA/RMW.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash funding of total investment outlay
critic_notes.rationale: A clean one-variable extension (capex → capex + acquisitions) that tests a substantively different notion of total capital deployment and correctly avoids the zero-mass problem of a standalone aqc ratio, but the denominator is dominated by capx so the marginal information over Signal 1 will likely be modest and confined to the serial-acquirer tail.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash buffer cover of investment and current obligations
critic_notes.rationale: With lct typically dwarfing capx, this collapses to a plain cash-to-current-liabilities ratio — a textbook liquidity measure and a close cousin of the documented cash-holdings return premium — so it is too trivial and too close to known anomalies to justify a slot, notwithstanding its value as a decomposition diagnostic.

critic_notes.target_name: Chronic-loss expansion
critic_notes.rationale: The ZSCORE centering of the loss count contradicts the stated hypothesis — below-average loss frequency yields a negative multiplier, so the signal actively predicts *higher* returns for high-capex profitable firms (against the investment anomaly) rather than the claimed "no penalty" — and structurally it is the archive's sign-flipped capacity-expansion signal with a loss-count gate swapped for the ROA gate.

critic_notes.target_name: Bounded output response to prior investment
critic_notes.rationale: The asset-scaling repair is the right response to the 1/capx pathology in the archive's Δsale/capx signal, but as a difference of two standardized legs it is a linear blend of two known predictors whose expected signs conflict — cross-sectional sales growth is documented as a *negative* return predictor while the capex leg largely reproduces CMA — so an aligned positive slope would be hard to attribute to the claimed output-response channel.

critic_notes.target_name: Retained-earnings backing of invested capital
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially retained-earnings-to-capital, a close relative of the published RE/assets and RE/market-equity quality measures and largely a proxy for cumulative profitability and firm age (likely absorbed by RMW), and the denominator is not "strictly positive" in practice — asset-light firms with near-zero ppegt+intan will generate explosive values that 1% winsorization will not tame.

critic_notes.target_name: Current-year resource cover of capex
critic_notes.rationale: This is a pure horizon re-parameterization of the archive leader (identical numerator/denominator with TS_SUM windows collapsed to one year), which is exactly the cosmetic-variant class the objective warns against, and the coverage gain is incidental rather than mechanistic.

critic_notes.target_name: Resource cover of capex and maturing debt
critic_notes.rationale: A defensible marginal refinement of the archive leader, but it adds a single-year stock (dlc) to a three-year flow sum, so the denominator mixes units and dlc's contribution is arbitrarily scaled down by the window length — precisely the reason it will look "capex-dominated" and likely just reproduce the parent signal.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash pile relative to investment requirement
critic_notes.rationale: Stripped of the cash-flow numerator this is cash holdings scaled by capital intensity, i.e. a close cousin of the well-documented cash-to-assets/cash-holdings return premium, and as an attribution exercise it is a decomposition of an existing archive signal rather than a new economic claim.

critic_notes.target_name: Resource cover of fixed and working capital investment
critic_notes.rationale: The denominator TS_SUM(capx + Δinvt, 3) is not sign-stable — inventory drawdowns can drive it toward zero or negative, flipping the ratio's sign for exactly the distressed/destocking firms the hypothesis cares about — and 1% winsorization will not repair that; the numerator also reverts to unadjusted cash earnings, undoing the accrual adjustment that generated the family's best evidence.

critic_notes.target_name: Improving funding adequacy of investment
critic_notes.rationale: The change-in-coverage form is a genuinely distinct information set from the levels the archive has tested and the sign logic is coherent, though the two-thirds overlap between consecutive three-year windows means the delta is driven almost entirely by the entering and exiting years and may be dominated by noise.

critic_notes.target_name: Sales per dollar of operating capital
critic_notes.rationale: This is capital turnover, a standard DuPont component whose return predictability is already published (Soliman 2008; Novy-Marx-style profitability/turnover work), and in this raw un-industry-adjusted form it will mostly load on industry capital intensity rather than on the idle-capacity mechanism the reasoning invokes.

critic_notes.target_name: Resource cover of capex and all debt
critic_notes.rationale: A legitimate discriminating ablation of the gen-4 leader that separates near-term refinancing pressure from a general leverage tilt, though adding `dltt` pushes the denominator toward a conventional cash-flow-to-total-debt coverage measure that overlaps known leverage/distress signals and risks being spanned by FF5.

critic_notes.target_name: Flow-only cover of capex and maturing debt
critic_notes.rationale: A clean, internally consistent component attribution (flow versus cash stock) with real economic stakes — precautionary liquidity is a distinct, separately documented effect — but it is a strict-subset ablation of an existing archive signal and so is informative rather than novel.

critic_notes.target_name: Unit-consistent smoothed cover of capex and maturing debt
critic_notes.rationale: The unit correction is real (annual-rate flows against a debt stock rather than three-year cumulations) and capex lumpiness is a genuine noise source, but this is a measurement refinement of the leader rather than a new mechanism, so the payoff is bounded to a t-stat improvement.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry-neutral cover of capex and maturing debt
critic_notes.rationale: Wrapping the existing leader in IND_ZSCORE is a mechanical normalization rather than a new economic claim, and the stated concern (industry composition of the spread) is more directly and cheaply diagnosed by inspecting leg industry weights than by spending a slot on a standard transform.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash generation per dollar of capital consumed
critic_notes.rationale: Since depreciation is roughly proportional to the capital base, this ratio is essentially cash-based operating profitability scaled by capital — a well-documented anomaly largely spanned by RMW/CMA — and it closely duplicates the archive's "Improving cash return on installed capital" and "Cash earnings coverage of capital spending"; the framing as a redirect of `capx/dp` also does not match what the expression computes, which is a profitability level rather than an investment-quality measure.

critic_notes.target_name: Equity-funded share of gross investment
critic_notes.rationale: This is close to a direct rediscovery of the external-financing / composite equity-issuance anomaly (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan; Pontiff-Woodgate), where financing raised is already routinely scaled by assets or investment, and `sstk` coverage plus its heavy skew toward small, loss-making issuers make it likely to reproduce a known issuance effect rather than the archive's funding-adequacy mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Rank-combined stock and flow coverage
critic_notes.rationale: Because (che + flow)/(capx+dlc) is exactly the sum of the two legs being rank-combined, this is a rank-weighting reparameterization of the archive's already-tested stock-plus-flow coverage signal rather than a new economic claim.

critic_notes.target_name: Smoothed cover of peak commitments
critic_notes.rationale: This merely swaps MA(capx,3) for TS_MAX(capx,3) in the existing generation-5 leader (alpha 7.1%, t=5.65), a highly correlated parameter tweak whose two "independent" denominators differ only in a 3-year smoothing statistic.

critic_notes.target_name: Coverage level plus buffer dynamics
critic_notes.rationale: The level/trajectory framing is coherent, but this is a rank blend of two already-evaluated archive signals — one of which carries a wrong-signed FMB slope (-0.83) — so it is portfolio stacking that will mostly reproduce the leader while diluting its cross-sectional evidence.

critic_notes.target_name: Volatility of resources relative to commitments
critic_notes.rationale: The second-moment idea is new to the family, but dividing by (capx+dlc) makes the signal mechanically large for low-commitment firms, so the negative expected sign directly contradicts the direction established by the coverage leaders and the result risks being an inverted commitment-intensity proxy plus the known cash-flow-volatility anomaly.

critic_notes.target_name: Persistence of self-funded investment
critic_notes.rationale: A genuinely different construction within the productive family — a monotone six-state count of self-funding years that tests durability versus level, is outlier-robust without winsorization, and avoids the degenerate-mask problem of the earlier failed INDICATOR signal.

critic_notes.target_name: Commitment intensity times coverage quality
critic_notes.rationale: Internally inconsistent: since ZSCORE is affine, multiplying by (capx+dlc)/at algebraically cancels the coverage denominator, so the expression collapses to roughly (che+cash flow)/at minus a multiple of commitment intensity — a cash-profitability-minus-investment composite, not the claimed magnitude-scaled quality interaction.

critic_notes.target_name: Tail-compressed cover of capex and maturing debt
critic_notes.rationale: This is the archive's gen-4 "Same-period cover of capex and maturing debt" with the winsorization parameter changed from 1% to 10% — the textbook definition of a cosmetic variant, and the stated concavity hypothesis could be tested far more informatively with a genuine transform (log, rank, or capped-at-1 coverage) than by re-running the same expression at a different trim.

critic_notes.target_name: Conservative resource cover of commitments
critic_notes.rationale: The MIN is likely degenerate — gross profit almost always exceeds cash earnings net of working-capital change for the typical firm, so the operator will select the cash-generation leg in the large majority of firm-years and the signal will collapse into a near-duplicate of the existing t=5.71 archive signal; the "prudence rule" only bites if the two legs are comparably scaled, which they are not.

critic_notes.target_name: Proportional coverage plus absolute spare capacity
critic_notes.rationale: Both legs share the identical numerator quantity (cash generation less capex and current debt) and differ only in scaling denominator, so this is a rank-space reweighting of two already-tested, mechanically correlated versions of the same construct rather than a new economic statement — and the proposal's own defense concedes a prior rank blend was already rejected on these grounds.

critic_notes.target_name: Self-funded and output-validated investment
critic_notes.rationale: The two legs are genuinely distinct economic channels (financing adequacy versus realized output response) and the depreciation floor is a defensible fix to the diagnosed 1/capex explosion, but be aware the output leg has now twice produced a *negatively* signed FMB slope, so a rank blend risks diluting the cross-sectional evidence the objective prizes — report leg-level slopes alongside the composite.

critic_notes.target_name: Commitment escalation per dollar of revenue
critic_notes.rationale: DELTA(capx)/sale is essentially the published abnormal-capital-investment/investment-growth anomaly and DELTA(dlc)/sale is the short-term component of the net-external-financing anomaly, so summing them is a mashup of two well-documented effects, and the sum is dimensionally awkward (a change in an annual expenditure flow added to a change in a balance-sheet stock) with no argument for equal weighting.

critic_notes.target_name: Worst-year surplus per dollar of assets
critic_notes.rationale: Applying TS_MIN to the asset-scaled surplus rather than the coverage ratio is a substantive normalization change with a clearly articulated diagnosis of why both prior durability attempts underperformed, though the result will be strongly correlated with the level of the asset-scaled surplus (fmb 3.54, alpha 4.3%) and may be driven by a stale worst year, so the incremental information over that leg should be verified directly.

critic_notes.target_name: Funding adequacy plus investment restraint
critic_notes.rationale: A defensible rank-blend of the archive's best alpha leg with its best slope leg, but the two legs are far less independent than claimed — capx sits in the denominator of leg one and the numerator of leg two, and dp appears in both — so much of the "restraint" information is already embedded in the coverage ratio, and the restraint leg's near-zero FF5 alpha (0.003, t=0.29) makes dilution as likely as improvement.

critic_notes.target_name: Three-channel investment quality composite
critic_notes.rationale: The stated justification is factually wrong ("all three legs share no variables" — capx, dp, sale and invt recur across legs), the nested SUMRANK silently weights the funding leg 50% versus 25% each for the others despite a hypothesis of three co-equal conditions, and the construct is the existing "Financing discipline plus operating utilization" (fmb 3.98, alpha 4.6%) plus an FF5-spanned third leg, so it is closer to a cosmetic extension than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Conjunctive three-channel quality screen
critic_notes.rationale: Testing MIN versus SUMRANK aggregation on identical economic content is a legitimate, non-affine design question with prior evidence that MIN works on well-measured legs, though a three-way minimum is fragile — the score is set by whichever z-score is noisiest, and one of the three legs (replacement-adjusted capex) has no standalone alpha.

critic_notes.target_name: Unadjusted cash earnings cover of commitments
critic_notes.rationale: A clean, well-motivated ablation that isolates whether the accrual adjustment still earns its keep once maturing debt enters the denominator, and it is distinct from the archive's lct-denominator version, though the stated hypothesis (accrual inflation is "offset" by short-term debt) is hand-waving and the honest framing is diagnostic rather than a new economic mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Redundant funding sources for commitments
critic_notes.rationale: The redundancy logic is genuinely non-affine and interesting, but because the cash-stock leg is bounded below at zero while the flow leg is frequently negative, the MIN will select the flow leg for most firms and the signal risks collapsing into the archive's existing "Flow-only cover of capex and maturing debt" (fmb 3.38, alpha 4.8%); the absence of WINSOR on ratios with a potentially near-zero capx+dlc denominator is an additional construction defect relative to the rest of the family.

critic_notes.target_name: Persistent-earnings cover plus utilization
critic_notes.rationale: A single-leg substitution into the archive's best joint-evidence composite is incremental, but it is a targeted test of which numerator pairs better with the utilization channel and it materially raises panel coverage, so it earns a slot despite being a variant rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Three-year cover of capex and maturing debt
critic_notes.rationale: A genuinely untested permutation within a heavily mined family with clear diagnostic purpose, but the stated "dimensional repair" is overstated since `dlc` is a balance-sheet stock and `TS_SUM(dlc,3)` only proxies three years of rollover under a strong assumption, while `che` remains a point-in-time stock against three-year flows.

critic_notes.target_name: Three-year unadjusted cover of capex and maturing debt
critic_notes.rationale: The motivating claim is economically wrong — `TS_SUM(DELTA(WC,1),3)` telescopes to the three-year *level* change in working capital, which grows systematically with the firm rather than washing out, so the accrual adjustment is if anything more consequential at this horizon — and stripped of that rationale the proposal is a minor ablation of an existing archive ratio.

critic_notes.target_name: High-coverage cover plus operating utilization
critic_notes.rationale: This is the third numerator swap in an already twice-evaluated SUMRANK pairing (accrual-adjusted leg fmb 3.98/alpha 4.6%, gross-profit leg fmb 2.65/alpha 3.8%), making it a cosmetic variant whose only differentiator is a ~2pp coverage gain rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Best single source cover plus utilization
critic_notes.rationale: Same SUMRANK template as prior archive entries, but the pairing is properly diagnosed — a high-alpha/weak-slope sufficiency leg combined with an orthogonal slope-strengthening channel — so the test has a defensible ex ante rationale rather than being arbitrary recombination.

critic_notes.target_name: Two-channel conjunctive screen
critic_notes.rationale: A well-motivated ablation that isolates which leg of the three-way MIN destroys alpha and, jointly with the already-evaluated additive version, cleanly separates conjunctive from averaging aggregation — the most informative test in this batch despite operating inside a saturated family.

critic_notes.target_name: High-coverage trough cover of commitments
critic_notes.rationale: Combining the trough numerator with the unadjusted cash-earnings simplification is a legitimate first-time pairing of two separately validated changes with a real coverage benefit, though it is a two-ingredient swap in an existing ratio and is mislabelled `novel` when it is plainly a ratio.
